A very well-designed bullet-hell shmup. It gets a little complicated in terms of scoring, alternate routes, hidden second loops, and three different TLBs, but the base game is still very fun.

Basic run-down of the different modes:
1.5: Main version of the game.
Black Label: One-loop only. Strong type is expert mode. You can use both your focus laser and your main shot at the same time which is more powerful and cancels an enemy's bullets upon killing it, but it will temporarily increase rank. Comes with an amazing alternate soundtrack.
Black Label Arrange: A mix of Black Label and Ketsui. Very fun if you like Ketsui's more aggressive scoring system. Plays a remix of Ketsui's soundtrack.
1.51: You are locked to the alternate (Ura) route and will face both Taisabachi and Hibachi regardless of how trash you are at the game (I speak from experience).
Don't worry about Arrange A and B. One of them is just a weird, overly convoluted rank-based thing where you choose whatever stage you want to play. The other lets you play with one of the ships from Daioujou.

One of the best if not the best (Crimzon Clover is a very strong contender) bullet hell shooters on Steam! If you are thinking that the price is too high, know that you'll get a ton of different modes and arranges in a single package with 3 different soundtrack track sets that you can customize per game stage. Fit for all skill levels from complete novices to superplayers.

Play on the lowest difficulty and do not worry about how many credits you needed to clear it. 

I felt discouraged from my first playthroughs being so bad but just kept playing. 

Lowkey feels like magic when you keep playing and realize you got to stage 3 without dying once and didn't even realize it. The growth feels natural.

There is no level up system, battle pass or any type of progression system but you level up your skill and expression with the game and that itself feels enriching vs just getting higher number values or climbing a chore ladder with all its challenges.

I miss more simpler games but has many layers and depth to its gameplay that you can explore over hundreds of hours. Very rewarding and timeless experience.

really decent port with TONS of content inside, as well as autobomb (previously, autobomb was available only in Black Label re-release and 1.5) with novice mode that make these titles much more manageable to players that aren't used to traditional danmaku STGs. 
Input lag as far as my experience can tell is pretty minimal too, so alongside tons of content you also get a comfortable way of experiencing all this content, especially given how you need to do some very precise movements during some moments.

Now, for the modes:
(not in steam port) - 1.0 release, original arcade version that was replaced with 1.5 in a few months. really the only mode this port lacks, which is kinda sad from preservation value...
1.5 Normal - an overhauled arcade release that has became a defenitive way of experiencing the game after 1.0 cabinets were removed due to a couple of bugs.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=97BKFry-yXI

(NOTE: in original 1.0 release, Type-B and Strong style were locked behind a specific input code, meanwhile while Type-B is available in 1.5 by default, you had to either 1cc the game or input a code to unlock it in arcade mode)

1.5 Novice - same as 1.5, but with a couple of changes, including easier patterns, bomb pickups fully refreshing your bomb stock and bees being always visible.
1.51 - an some sort of "arrange" mode, where you're forcefully put in a some sort of Ura loop (basically, you encounter True Final Boss), alongside much more lenient scoring mechanics and hypers that become worse at clearing bullets with each hyper used
Arrange A - a arrange where you get through game with ship from DoDonPachi DaiOuJou, with mechanics from that game.
Arrange B - weird arrange where you go through individual stages for high scores.
Black Label - a re-release of game that aimed at fixing the balance, that also makes game slightly harder.
Black Label Novice - same as Black Label, but with tweaks from novice mode that make game easier.
Black Label Arrange (also known as KetsuiPachi) - a mode that was exclusive to X360 port, which combined chip system of Ketsui (as well as locked you into powerful wide ship from Ketsui) and chaining mechanics of Dai-FukkaTsu, as well as contains some AMAZING remixes of tracks from Ketsui. Probably closest thing to Ketsui on PC we'll get in a while too.

DoDonPachi Resurrection é um intenso shoot 'em up (shmup) da Cave, lançado originalmente em 2008 nos arcades japoneses. O game é a continuação espiritual de DoDonPachi Dai-Ou-Jou e leva ao extremo a fórmula de combates aéreos frenéticos, repletos de balas inimigas na tela, no clássico estilo "bullet hell".

Visualmente, o jogo impressiona com gráficos vibrantes em 2D, explosões espetaculares e uma enxurrada de projéteis em padrões hipnóticos. O sistema de combo é fundamental para pontuações altas, exigindo precisão e reflexos afiados. O jogador pode escolher entre diferentes naves e modos de ataque, cada um com vantagens estratégicas específicas.

A trilha sonora eletrônica mantém a adrenalina alta o tempo todo. Apesar da dificuldade elevada, Resurrection é justo, com controles responsivos e uma curva de aprendizado desafiadora, mas recompensadora. Para fãs de shmups, é uma obra-prima imperdível.

Происходящее на экране вызывает восхищение и захватывает дух. Всё взрывается, монетки валятся, паттерны гипнотизируют, корабль под гипером даёт ощущение подлинного могущества, комбинации достигают трёхзначных значений, огромный лазер прорезает экран и, кажется, вот-вот расплавит уровень, меха-вайфу-боссы доставляют. Хитбокс корабля очень маленький, часто случаются такие увороты, что дух захватывает. Несмотря на ад на экране, игра хороша, чтобы расслабиться, особенно под отличную музыку. Пятый уровень настолько интенсивный и длинный, что первые четыре ощущаются как разминка и фарм ресурсов перед настоящей игрой. Судя по тренировке на уровнях есть роутинг и дополнительные уровни, но я пока не понял что да как. Чем больше играю, тем больше удивляют продуманности игры и мелким деталям.
